agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (iv) inline process bodies not validated
summary_for_principal:
This closes another checklist item from a past session (as with the last item, the original investigation's detail was lost to context compression, so I re-verified from scratch).

A tool can embed its own small self-contained process instead of calling a separately defined one. That embedded process was never checked for correctness at all — a broken one (a starting point that doesn't exist, a route to nowhere, a reference to an unregistered tool) passed every check and only failed the first time someone actually ran it, with a confusing internal error instead of a clear one up front.

Fixed by running the same correctness checks on an embedded process that already apply to a standalone one. While testing, I found a real example of this exact problem already sitting in the specification's own reference example — a value read and written that was never declared. Fixed that too, in both the spec text and the matching test file.

Full test suite: 380 passed, 4 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. One item remains from the original list, plus two larger leftover pieces of an earlier item.

also.reason: New regression tests: an accepted well-formed inline body, a refused undeclared-ending case, a refused undeclared-tool-reference case, and a fixture-level regression confirming the real corpus example is now clean.

D35 added to §18 (MADR form); §9.1's own worked example snippet corrected to match the fixture fix.

decisions.problem: InlineProcess shares start/nodes/state/endings with Process, but validate_tool never recursed into mechanism.process at all — confirmed by grep (mechanism.process appears nowhere in validate.py before this fix) and by construction (a start: naming no node in its own nodes passes with zero findings, surfacing only as an uncaught EngineRefusal at runtime).
options_rejected: Write bespoke recursive-walking logic scoped to InlineProcess's own reduced shape: rejected — InlineProcess is already duck-type compatible with every rule function this pass reuses, so bespoke logic would only duplicate what already exists correctly.

Reuse V10's self-reachability/depth check too, giving the synthetic wrapper a placeholder header.id: rejected — V10's check is keyed off a registered Process's header.id inside a registry-wide call graph, and an anonymous inline body has no id anything else could ever name to call it; forcing it through would either silently no-op or need a new, spec-silent definition of self-reachability for an anonymous body.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — _validate_inline_process is additive (a new function plus one call site); the fixture/spec correction is a two-line addition with no behavioural change to anything that already worked.
